classification.difficultyReason: Identify triangular and trapezoidal regions from supplied graphs, then negate the results when integration limits are reversed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate these definite integrals using graphs and area formulae.

spec.description: Descending straight line on unnumbered axes; both axes and the line have arrowheads at both ends. Width accommodates the source three-column arrangement.
spec.mathematics: The line is y=1-4x, crossing the y-axis at 1 and x-axis at 1/4. Intercepts are not labelled in the supplied graph.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; no bounds, shading or numerical answers added.

answer.worked:
The region is a triangle above the $x$-axis. Its base is $\frac14-(-\frac14)=\frac12$ and its height is $1-4(-\frac14)=2$.
$$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\frac14}^{\frac14}(1-4x)\,dx&=\frac12\times\frac12\times2\\&=\frac12.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: V-shaped absolute-value graph on unnumbered axes, with vertex on the negative x-axis. Both axes and both outer graph ends have arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: y=|x+5| has vertex (-5,0) and crosses the y-axis at 5. No numerical ticks or intercept labels are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; no working or shaded answer region.

answer.worked:
The region is a triangle above the $x$-axis, with base $1-(-5)=6$ and height $|1+5|=6$.
$$\begin{aligned}\int_{-5}^{1}|x+5|\,dx&=\frac12\times6\times6\\&=18.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: V-shaped graph symmetric about the y-axis, with vertex above the origin. Unnumbered axes and outer graph ends have arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: y=|x|+3 has vertex (0,3). The source graph has no numerical labels or ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; no integration bounds or answer shading added.

answer.worked:
The region is a trapezium above the $x$-axis. Its parallel vertical sides have lengths $3$ and $|2|+3=5$, separated by $2$.
$$\begin{aligned}\int_0^2(|x|+3)\,dx&=\frac12(3+5)\times2\\&=8.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence write down the value of:

answer.worked:
Reversing the limits negates the integral.
$$\begin{aligned}\int_{\frac14}^{-\frac14}(1-4x)\,dx&=-\int_{-\frac14}^{\frac14}(1-4x)\,dx\\&=-\frac12.\end{aligned}$$

Reversing the limits negates the integral.
$$\begin{aligned}\int_1^{-5}|x+5|\,dx&=-\int_{-5}^1|x+5|\,dx\\&=-18.\end{aligned}$$

Reversing the limits negates the integral.
$$\begin{aligned}\int_2^0(|x|+3)\,dx&=-\int_0^2(|x|+3)\,dx\\&=-8.\end{aligned}$$
